title: Hyperautomation & Systems Integration
breadcrumb: Services > Agentic AI & Hyperautomation > Hyperautomation & Systems Integration
meta_description: Hyperautomation & Systems Integration from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: The honest pitch for hyperautomation & systems integration fits in a sentence — One automation spine — APIs, events, RPA and agents composable under common control. — and the rest of this page is the how: measured baseline, bounded build, evidence in flight.

Most enterprises run four automation technologies as four kingdoms: APIs, event streams, RPA and now agents, each with its own tools, logs and risk reviews. We build the integration spine that makes them composable — an event backbone (Kafka-class), an API mesh with contracts, a governed RPA layer for systems without APIs, and agent tooling that consumes the same contracts — all under one control plane with unified logging and policy.

The payoff shows up in change absorption: when the core system changes, one contract update propagates to every consumer, human or agent. We include the migration discipline for legacy RPA estates — inventory, refactor-or-retire decisions, and consolidation onto the spine — which typically cuts automation run cost by a third while improving auditability.

The sectors where Hyperautomation & Systems Integration currently runs: Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Telecom, Media & Entertainment, Manufacturing & Industrial. Each engagement anchors to one named metric in that sector's own language.
